input.rationale: First pass: L=1um everywhere for gain headroom, Cc/CL=0.3 and p2=3*GBW for PM margin, SR 60 V/us.
Gain predicted 77 dB vs 43 dB simulated: lambda was 4.8x (n) and 2.1x (p) too optimistic. kn/vthn not usable: M1 in triode.
Same knobs with recalibrated lambda to see the real gain gap; vin_max 1.0 V to widen M3/M4 and give M1/M2 Vds headroom.
Gain: lengthen NMOS only (lambda_n ~2.3x lambda_p): l1=l5=2um, PMOS stay 1um to keep M6 small. GBW: Cc/CL 0.6 so Cc dominates the first-stage parasitic.
M1/M2 now saturated: real vthn 0.257 V (not 0.4) changes the M3 headroom equation; kn 0.27 mA/V2. lam_n NOT taken: M2 only 55 mV above Vdsat inflates gds.
With true vthn the vin_max=1.0 condition widens M3/M4 (lower Vsg3, more Vds for M1/M2). p2/GBW 3->4 to recover PM lost to first-stage parasitics.
M2 and M7 now well above Vdsat (0.40 V / 0.80 V), so lambda_n extraction is trustworthy: 0.49 um/V. Gain was over-predicted by 9 dB.
Cut first-stage parasitic: PMOS L 1->0.5um (4x less gate area for same W/L); vin_max 0.95 so M3/M6 are less weakly inverted; p2/GBW back to 3. Recover gain with NMOS L 2.5um.
D5 predicts 58 dB: compromise PMOS L 0.7um (still ~2x less gate area than 1um) and NMOS L 3.5um to get about +3 dB per stage.
PM/GBW limited by first-stage parasitic C1 and Rz fixed at 1/gm6. Make Cc dominate C1: Cc/CL 0.6->1.0 (real GBW closer to gm1/Cc, p2 toward gm6/(C1+CL)); p2/GBW 3.5. Power budget allows it.
Probe: p2/GBW 5 and Cc/CL 1.5, same lengths. Check power before simulating.
Probe: p2/GBW 5, Cc/CL 1.0, NMOS L back to 2.5um to shrink the input pair (accept ~1 dB gain loss; Cc dominance helps less than expected).
Keep D7 lengths (gain margin is thin), raise p2/GBW 3.5->5: CL still dominates the output node, so more gm6 should still raise p2.

PM tracks the PMOS mirror (34 deg at gm/Id 16, 46 at 12) -> mirror pole at x1. vin_max 0.9 makes M3/M4 narrower (lower gm/Id, higher fT). SR 60->45 lowers I5 with same gm1: M1 gm/Id ~14 recovers stage-1 gain and saves power.
Probe: D9 + Rz cancelling p2 (rz_ratio = 1+CL/Cc = 2).
Probe: p2/GBW 3.5 (smaller M6, less C1 and power) with rz_ratio 2.
Probe: p2/GBW 3.5 with stronger LHP zero rz_ratio 3 to also cover the unmodelled mirror pole.
D12 PM 59, GBW 44: equations cannot rank rz beyond cancellation (no p3/mirror pole), so step rz_ratio to 3.5; the LHP zero should add phase and lift |A| near UGF.
Gain over-predicted by 4 dB; lambda*L is not constant in SG13G2, so take values measured at the lengths now in use (NMOS 3.5um, PMOS 0.7um). All devices well saturated.
D14 meets spec with 0.1 dB gain margin. Trade GBW/PM margin for gain: PMOS L 0.7->1.0um; rz_ratio 3.5 keeps the LHP zero.
Reference: D14 knobs under the recalibrated lambda, to read the gain change of the PMOS L step from the equations.
Longer PMOS costs 17 deg PM (mirror pole). Take gain from the input pair instead: D14 with SR 50 -> I5 100uA, M1 gm/Id ~12.7 (+~1.6 dB stage 1, less power). M2 has 138 mV saturation margin to spend.
Same direction once more for gain margin: SR 45 -> M1 gm/Id ~14. Risk: wider M1 adds capacitance and GBW margin is only 5%.
